MAIN LINE · RECOMMENDED

Real Dex1-1 gripper

One of the two ordered grippers on the VR controller, driven from the controller trigger. The second stays on the UR10e.

How it works

  • Trigger → PC → RS-485 → gripper
  • Printed adapter under the grip
  • Precedent: ActiveUMI, RAPID

Gripper signal

  • + Identical metal fingers
  • + Command, position, torque at 500 Hz
  • − Needs angle-to-width calibration

Mass and power

  • − ≈ 846 g incl. controller (CAD)
  • − 24–64 V, 3.5 A peak, powered cable
  • UMI 780 g · UMI-3D 1120 g

Before delivery

  • Printed dummy gripper: size, fit, LED visibility
  • Software against a simulated gripper
Next choice on this path: trigger mapping, proportional vs open/close. Both are tested.
DOCUMENTED FALLBACK

Printed copy

Passive printed copy of the Dex1-1 mechanism, closed by a squeeze trigger. Design from the original proposal.

How it works

  • Rack and pinion on MGN9 rails
  • Squeeze trigger, rigid link ≈ 4:1
  • Precedent: UMI, RDT2, TacUMI

Gripper signal

  • − Width only (marker or encoder)
  • − No command, no force
  • − Printed fingers differ from metal

Mass and power

  • + ≈ 438 g, still rising (CAD)
  • + Unpowered, camera USB only
  • − Grip span 54–64 mm vs 45–55 mm optimum

Design state

  • Mechanism, trigger, link designed
  • Gripper bracket still open
  • Testable once printed and rails bought

Common to both

  • PICO 4 Ultra controller as the handle
  • RGB camera on the gripper, tethered PC
  • Size and stroke from the official CAD
  • UR10e: flange plate and external supply

Open points

  • Communication check only possible after delivery
  • Stroke 82–83 mm (CAD) vs 90 mm (product page)
  • Handheld mass: operator fatigue untested

Not decided here

  • Observed vs commanded arm pose as action
  • Tracking accuracy, deployment compliance
